doc.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Uncle Nathaniel the bass singer and church singing
summary: His youngest uncle Nathaniel sang bass in the choir; no one played an instrument and singing happened only in church.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: My mother was musically inclined. I had an uncle who sang in the choir, and as I said, they all went to church and sang – the whole congregation. But I had one uncle – the youngest uncle – Nathaniel, the youngest one. He was a bass singer. He sang bass. He was in the choir.
Your mother sang? Did she play an instrument or anything like that?

People often talk about their being family gatherings in the South and singing at Thanksgiving or dinners. Was there that kind of – were those kind of things happening in your home, where people would gather and sing spirituals or anything like that?
No. No, I didn’t have that. All the singing was done pretty much in the church.
And long hours in the church I think.
